t: The Celtiberians were a group of Celtic-speaking peoples, including the Arevaci and Belli, living in fortified towns on the plateau of central Spain.
Famed as warriors and sword-makers, they served as mercenaries and resisted Rome in a series of wars from 181 to 133 BCE.
The fall of Numantia in 133 BCE broke their independence, and after the Sertorian War they were absorbed into Roman Spain.
dyk: The poet Catullus mocked a Celtiberian named Egnatius for brushing his teeth with urine, a custom that the historian Diodorus Siculus also reported among the Celtiberians.
ev: Celtiberian mercenaries desert the Scipio brothers, contributing to their defeat
Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus ends the First Celtiberian War with treaties
The Belli under Carus ambush and defeat the consul Quintus Fulvius Nobilior
Numantia forces the consul Gaius Hostilius Mancinus to surrender with about 20,000 men
Scipio Aemilianus starves Numantia into surrender and razes it
The Tabula Contrebiensis records a land dispute settled at Contrebia Belaisca
Pompey ends the Sertorian War and reduces the last Celtiberian towns

f.capital: No single capital; leading towns Numantia, Segeda, Termes and Contrebia Belaisca
